english: Dawn, bright goddess, hear us, you who split the night, you who lead the sun. Give light to this man's eyes and heal his sore. May the sun's wheel carry the anguish away. Dry the blood, and let him wake. May he live and see your light again.
uncertain: skélHs 'you split/cut open' (aor. 2sg of *skelH-) taken as 'who cut through the night'
subject of bʰéwdʰtu assumed to be the man

english: Night came and the clan chief lay down. Thief, do not come to the clan chief's door. May your two eyes not see. Now, thief, may your arm go slack. The dog is awake and the god guards the homestead. Whoever steals cattle, may he die.
uncertain: ḱóymom: lexicon has both 'homely' (adj.) and 'village'; read as 'home, village'

english: The spear struck me in the head. My blood goes out. I lie down, and it grows dark. Worms will swallow my bones. Tell my sister: he fell by the spear. Do not weep; my name will be famous.
uncertain: h₁éǵʰs taken as the adverb/preverb 'out' (not in the token index)

english: The horses lay in the field and did not stand. The Lady sat by them and kindled a fire. Then dawn broke. She looked at them and said: 'Stand up and do not be afraid.' Then they stood up and went forth.

Earth, take my brother and protect him. Brother, lie down at the oak. The oak's roots will pierce your bones. You (pl.!) grew up on the rock; now you lie down. May Perkunos know your name; may your name not vanish.
uncertain: h₂uksté is 2pl (aor./imp.) though the addressee is one brother: looks like a person/number error
péruti read as loc. 'on the rock/mountain' (not in index)
widyéh₁t is the optative of the perfect *woyde 'know', so 'know' rather than 'see'

english: Fire, burn the grubs in the wool. Burn the worms, burn the eggs. Do not burn the wool, do not burn the seat. Sheep's wool, become white. Now the man smears it with honey. The grubs that are in it will die.
uncertain: sédos 'seat' is odd in a wool charm (maybe 'the place where it lies')
h₁ésmi is m./n. loc. 'in it' while wool is feminine
h₂éwis read as gen. 'of the sheep', not nom. 'bird'
